NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE: material modification (e.g., coated metal or corrosion-resistant alloys) to passively resist corrosion.  
Departure: Electrochemically active surface modification using a sacrificial metal oxide layer that dynamically redistributes charge during transients, mitigating anodic dissolution.  
Failure-physics connection: Bipolar plate corrosion during start-stop transients is driven by localized high-current-density anodic sites; the sacrificial oxide layer provides an alternative anodic reaction pathway, reducing metal dissolution kinetics by diverting current.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Corrosion rate (mm/year) = (K × i_corr × EW) / (ρ × n), where K = 3.27×10³ (mm·g·μA⁻¹·cm⁻¹·year⁻¹), i_corr = corrosion current density (μA/cm²), EW = equivalent weight (g/eq), ρ = density (g/cm³), n = valence.  
Magnitude verification: For stainless steel (EW=27.92, ρ=7.9, n=2), i_corr=10 μA/cm² yields 0.058 mm/year; with the oxide layer reducing i_corr to 1 μA/cm², corrosion drops to 0.0058 mm/year (90% reduction).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
Components:  
- Thin-film sacrificial oxide coating (e.g., TiO₂ or WO₃, 100–200 nm thickness) applied via ALD (ALREADY-RECORDED: "deposition process" from manufacturing logs).  
- Conductive underlayer (e.g., CrN, 500 nm) for adhesion (ALREADY-RECORDED: "surface preparation" records).  
Instruments:  
- Potentiostat (ALREADY-RECORDED: "electrochemical test cell" from QA logs).  
- pH sensor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "anode outlet pH" from operational telemetry).  
- Conductivity probe (ALREADY-RECORDED: "electrolyte conductivity" from process control system).  
Procedure:  
1. Deposit oxide coating via ALD (ALREADY-RECORDED: "coating thickness" from deposition logs).  
2. Verify coating integrity via cyclic voltammetry (ALREADY-RECORDED: "CV scan" from commissioning data).  
References:  
- Coating thickness threshold: 100 nm (CALCULATED: from "ALD deposition rate" (0.1 nm/cycle) × "spec cycles" (1000 cycles)).  
- pH threshold: 2.5 (CALCULATED: from "operating pH range" (2–3) + "safety margin" (0.5)).  
- Conductivity threshold: 100 mS/cm (CALCULATED: from "baseline conductivity" (150 mS/cm) × "min acceptable" (67%)).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as coating application (no new tooling; ALD already used in fuel cell manufacturing).  
- Operability: No change (no active control; passive operation).  
- Maintenance: Same (no added servicing; coating lifetime matches plate life).  
- Cost class: Same (ALD process cost offset by reduced material thickness; no net increase).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Subject coated plates to 100 start-stop cycles (0.1–1.0 A/cm², 25°C) with pH/conductivity logged.  
Pass/fail: Coating is valid if post-test i_corr (measured via polarization) is ≤10% of uncoated baseline.  
Duration: 72 hours (100 cycles at 40 min/cycle).  
Kill criterion: Mechanism is falsified if i_corr reduction is <90% (i.e., i_corr >1 μA/cm²).  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: Corrosion current density (i_corr), as it directly defines the failure threshold (metal dissolution rate). Secondary indicators (pH, conductivity) supplement by confirming electrolyte conditions but do not replace i_corr.  

DESIGN_POINT  
The oxide layer reduces i_corr by 90% (from 10 μA/cm² to 1 μA/cm²), extending bipolar plate lifespan from 5 years to 50 years under start-stop cycling.  

CLOSEST PRIOR ART  
Standard practice uses passive coatings (e.g., gold or graphite) that block corrosion but lack dynamic response to transients.  

DISTINGUISHING FEATURE  
The sacrificial oxide layer electrochemically redistributes charge during transients, providing active anodic protection instead of passive blocking.  

OBJECTIVE TECHNICAL PROBLEM  
Reduces localized anodic dissolution during current spikes by diverting current to the oxide layer, preventing pit initiation.  

WHY THE OBVIOUS KNOB FAILS  
Thicker passive coatings increase resistance and reduce conductivity, worsening transient performance; the oxide layer maintains conductivity while actively mitigating corrosion.
